brief: Goldman's rates note reads the past week's Fed, BoE, and BoJ decisions as reinforcing near-term curve flattening while leaving steepening on hold until markets gain clarity on how many hikes remain. The Fed hiked unanimously with hawkish signals (more projections for a further hike, a higher median dot, Chair Warsh's view the starting point isn't restrictive), so GS economists now expect another hike in October; market pricing already implies roughly three more hikes by mid-2027, above GS's baseline and the hawkish end of the Fed dots. That backdrop favors selling 3m30y USD straddles over outright duration, and GS expects policy to weigh more durably on long-end than front-end US inflation forwards. In Europe, the ECB's hawkish reaction function to energy prices is insulating belly forwards, supporting long EUR 1y1y vs CHF; GS still expects a November BoE hike despite the BoE's new Gilt-friendly QT plan (APF holdings to £120bn by 2034) compressing term premium, and forecasts Norges Bank and Riksbank hikes. The BoJ hiked 25bp but two dissents from Takaichi appointees disappointed hawkish expectations, so GS still recommends paying 5s on the JPY 2s5s10s fly.
